title: Senior Director of Site Operations at nVent Electric Sees Standardization as AVC’s Biggest Long-Term Competitive Risk
expert: Senior Director of Site Operations at nVent Electric (CDU and manifold competitor); AVC view is mostly market hearsay
verdict: A manifold competitor sees 2027 liquid-cooling volume already booked and manifold prices not falling, but names standardization (high-single-digit annual cost-downs) as AVC's biggest long-term risk.

Rubin yield and ramp: 🟢 Rubin yield 60–70% to ~80% (hearsay) vs ~60% in May (SB #64479). → Tenet 1 (Rubin content and share) ↑
Nvidia content and share: 🔴 Auras ~4% to over 10% cold-plate share (hearsay) vs 5–10% on GB (SB #64467). → Tenet 1 (Rubin content and share) ↓
Gross margin: 🔴 High-single-digit annual cost-downs under standardization, ~50% over several years (estimate), first read. → Tenet 3 (GM 34%+) ↓

changes: Auras cold-plate share >10% (hearsay) vs 5-10% on Nvidia GB (SB #64467): Auras gaining.
Rubin yield ~80% (hearsay) vs ~60% in May (SB #64479): improving.
First read on manifold pricing (not dropped over prior few years); no earlier expert call or stored row.
thesis_impact: Tenet 1 (Rubin content and share): → — hard to displace for 6-12 months, but Auras >10% share.
Tenet 3 (GM 34%+): ↓ — standardization could bring high-single-digit annual cost-downs.
Tenet 4 (capacity): ↑ — required cooling capacity doubling and tripling; 2027 volume booked.
